name: Ruins of Alterac
summary: Snow lies over the Ruins of Alterac, where Crushridge ogres now hold the old mountain capital. After King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Alliance in the Second War, Alterac was cast out and placed under martial law.

sections.title: A Kingdom's Betrayal
sections.body:
Alterac once ruled as an independent human realm, carved from the old Arathor empire and set high on mountain trade routes. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde feared the invading Old Horde would destroy his kingdom, so he secretly made a pact with the orcs. After the fighting at Caer Darrow, the betrayal came to light. The Alliance of Lordaeron struck swiftly.

King Terenas Menethil II placed the city under martial law and deposed Perenolde. The people fled or turned to outlawry, and the grand fortifications, church, and palace fell into disrepair.

sections.title: The Ogre Occupation
sections.body:
Surviving Alteraci nobles and rogue soldiers formed the Syndicate. They waged guerrilla campaigns from towns like Strahnbrad, but lost their ancestral capital. Today, Crushridge ogres under Mug'thol dwell among broken ramparts, palace halls, and wrecked ballistae. Neither the Syndicate nor Southshore's human defenders have reclaimed the fallen city.

Its crumbling towers and abandoned vaults remain dangerous ground for treasure hunters and scavengers.

faq.answer: During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde allied with the invading Orcish Horde, hoping to spare his kingdom. The Alliance of Lordaeron uncovered his treason and struck swiftly. Its forces invaded Alterac City, dismantled its defenses, and placed the kingdom under martial law.

faq.q: Who lives in the ruins now?
faq.answer: The Crushridge ogres, led by Mug'thol, have overtaken the palace, walls, and snowed-in courtyards. Bro'kin, an enterprising goblin alchemy vendor, sits quietly atop the northern ramparts.

faq.q: What is the Syndicate's connection to this place?
faq.answer: The Syndicate is made up largely of former Alteraci aristocracy and soldiers who lost their lands when the kingdom was dissolved. They bitterly long to reclaim Alterac, but the Crushridge ogres drove them from the capital. Now they operate from outposts like Strahnbrad.

faq.q: Why do Alliance adventurers come here?
faq.answer: Alliance soldiers from Southshore offer bounties on the hostile Crushridge ogres, who raid the roads. Nobles in the south, including Count Remington Ridgewell, also send agents into the ruins to recover lost family heirlooms like the Perenolde Tiara.

faq.q: Why is the Horde interested in these ruins?
faq.answer: Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken take an active interest in artifacts scattered across the fallen human kingdom. They send champions into the ogre-infested stronghold to secure relics of power such as the Crown of Will.

angles.text: As a human of the Alliance, these ruins recall human weakness and treason during the Second War. Perenolde's cowardice broke the brotherhood of the Seven Kingdoms.
As a member of the Horde, you hear echoes of the Old Horde's former alliances in this fallen city. The Forsaken can scavenge magical relics while the Crushridge ogres are distracted.
